title: Love Languages Quiz (Spouse)
description: A forced-choice quiz where you pick which of two statements is more meaningful to you in your relationship, to discover your primary and secondary love language.
instructions: For each pair, pick the statement that's more meaningful to you in your relationship, even if both sound true. Answer for the majority of the time, not just today.

scoring.method: count how many times each language was picked across all 30 questions; highest count = primary love language, second-highest = secondary (a tie means "bilingual" in that pair)

words.title: Words of Affirmation
words.description: You feel most loved through spoken and written encouragement — hearing appreciation, praise, and affection said out loud or in writing.
tips: Say the specific thing you appreciate, not just "good job" — specificity lands harder
A short note left somewhere they'll find it can mean as much as saying it in person
Avoid sarcasm or teasing about sensitive topics — words cut both ways for this language
Verbal affirmation in front of others (family, friends) especially reinforces the feeling

time.title: Quality Time
time.description: You feel most loved through focused, undistracted time together — presence matters more to you than words or gifts.
tips: Put phones away during shared time — partial attention doesn't register as quality time
Regular, smaller check-ins matter more than one big event a year
Ask about their day and actually follow up on details later — it shows you were present
Protect recurring time together, even 15-20 minutes daily, over occasional long stretches

service.title: Acts of Service
service.description: You feel most loved when someone does something helpful for you, especially without being asked — actions carry more weight than words.
tips: Notice what's overwhelming them and just take it off their plate
Follow through fully on promised help — a half-done task can feel worse than none
Ask what would actually help rather than guessing, since effort matters more than the specific task
Complaining while helping cancels out the gesture for this language — the spirit matters

gifts.title: Receiving Gifts
gifts.description: You feel most loved through thoughtful tangible tokens — not about cost, but about being remembered and thought of.
tips: Small, frequent, thoughtful gifts land better than one expensive annual gift
Remembering an offhand comment ("I love ___") and acting on it later is high-impact
Never regift or grab something last-minute — the thoughtfulness is the actual gift
Handmade or personal gifts often mean more than store-bought for this language

touch.title: Physical Touch
touch.description: You feel most loved through physical closeness and affection — touch communicates security and love more directly than words for you.
tips: Small consistent touches (hand on the back, a hug hello) matter as much as big romantic gestures
Physical distance during conflict can feel especially painful — try to stay physically connected even when upset
Non-sexual affection (sitting close, resting a head on a shoulder) is just as important as romantic touch
Ask before assuming what kind of touch is welcome, especially around others
